content.title: Sinclair, Nexstar Will Bring Kimmel Back to Their ABC Affiliates
content.summary: Sinclair  and  Nexstar Media Group  are putting  Jimmy Kimmel  back on the air.  The TV broadcasters, which combined own and operate more than 60 ABC affiliates in markets including Washington, D.C., New Orleans, Seattle and St. Louis, will end their pre-emption of “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” and air the late-night show again beginning Friday.  ABC suspended the show earlier this month after remarks Kimmel made about the killing of conservative activist and podcast host  Charlie Kirk.

content.title: Sinclair ends Kimmel boycott: What this illustrates about linear TV
content.description:
Sinclair Broadcast Group (SBGI) ended its boycott of ABC's Jimmy Kimmel Live! on Friday after the titular late night host returned from his suspension on Tuesday. Earlier this week, the broadcast company teamed with Nexstar Media Group (NXST) to air news over the show on their local stations.

Yahoo Finance senior media reporter Allie Canal highlights linear TV's fragility in this case of broadcaster backlash. LightShed Partners media analyst Rich Greenfield made the case to Yahoo Finance as to why Disney (DIS) could spin-off ABC.

Hear why Needham & Company's Laura Martin thinks Disney should just shut down ABC in an interview with Yahoo Finance earlier this week.

Plex CEO Keith Valory also commented that media companies have a "moral obligation" to uphold free speech practices against government pressures.

content.title: Should Disney spin off ABC over Kimmel broadcast pressures?
content.description:
Jimmy Kimmel Live! returned to ABC airways on Tuesday after being temporarily suspended for the late night host's political comments following the assassination of Charlie Kirk. Nexstar Media Group (NXST) and Sinclair Broadcast Group (SBGI) have united in boycotting Jimmy Kimmel's show from broadcasting on their local station.

LightShed Partners partner and media & technology analyst Rich Greenfield weighs in on Disney's (DIS) ownership of ABC while facing broadcast pressures.

Hear why Needham & Company's Laura Martin thinks Disney should just shut down ABC in an interview with Yahoo Finance earlier this week. Plex CEO Keith Valory also commented that media companies have a "moral obligation" to uphold free speech practices against government pressures.
